result.topic_en: Euler seeks rational solutions of $ss = \frac{xyp(x+y)}{xy-pp}$ by substitutions (Casus I, Casus II, and an alternative method), then works an example of the first case whose resulting product and sum he finds to be wrong ('falsa!').
result.transcription:
240 L. EULERI OPERA POSTHUMA. Arithmetica.
Ponatur porro $x = nqq$ et $y = nrr$, fietque
$ss = \frac{n^3 qqrrp(qq+rr)}{nnqqrr - pp}$, sive $\frac{ss}{nnqqrr} = \frac{np(qq+rr)}{nnqqrr - pp}$.
Ponatur nunc $nqr - p = k(qq+rr)$ eritque $p = nqr - k(qq+rr)$, ergo
$\frac{ss}{nnqqrr} = \frac{nnqr - nk(qq+rr)}{k(2nqr - k(qq+rr))} = \frac{n(k(qq+rr) - nqr)}{k(k(qq+rr) - 2nqr)}$.
Casus I. Sit $n = 2k$, erit $\frac{ss}{nnqqrr} = \frac{qq+rr-2qr}{qq+rr-4qr} = \frac{(q-r)^2}{qq+rr-4qr}$.
Sicque quadratum esse debet $qq+rr-4qr$, cujus radix ponatur $q + \frac{f}{g}r$, ita ut fiat
$rr - 4qr = \frac{2f}{g}qr + \frac{ff}{gg}rr$, vel $ggr - 4ggq = 2fgq + ffr$,
vel $(gg-ff)r = (4gg+2fg)q$, sive $\frac{q}{r} = \frac{gg-ff}{4gg+2fg}$.
Sumatur ergo $q = gg - ff$ et $r = 4gg + 2fg$, eritque
$\frac{ss}{nnqqrr} = \frac{(q-r)^2}{(q+\frac{f}{g}r)^2}$, ideoque $\frac{s}{nqr} = \frac{q-r}{q+\frac{f}{g}r} = \frac{3gg+ff+2fg}{gg+ff+4fg}$ et $s = \frac{2k(gg-ff)(4gg+2fg)(3gg+ff+2fg)}{gg+ff+4fg}$.
Quocirca erit $p = 2kqr - k(qq+rr) = -k(q-r)^2$, ideoque $x = 2kqq$, $y = 2krr$, $z = \frac{(x+y)pp}{xy-pp}$.
Casus II. Sumatur $n = k$, erit $\frac{ss}{kkqqrr} = \frac{qq+rr-qr}{(q-r)^2}$. Sit $\sqrt{(qq+rr-qr)} = q + \frac{f}{g}r$, erit
$rr - qr = \frac{2f}{g}qr + \frac{ff}{gg}rr$, vel $ggr - ggq = 2fgq + ffr$, hinc $\frac{q}{r} = \frac{gg-ff}{gg+2fg}$.
Sumatur ergo $q = gg - ff$ et $r = gg + 2fg$, ita ut sit
$\frac{s}{kqr} = \frac{q+\frac{f}{g}r}{q-r} = \frac{gg+fg+ff}{ff+2fg}$; hincque erit
$p = kqr - k(qq+rr)$, vel $p = k(qr - qq - rr)$, indeque $y = krr$, $x = kqq$, $z = \frac{(x+y)pp}{xy-pp}$.
Aliter. Cum sit $ss = \frac{xyp(x+y)}{xy-pp}$, dividetur per $xy$, eritque $ss = \frac{p(x+y)}{1-\frac{pp}{xy}}$. Sumatur $p = \frac{2xy}{x+y}$, fietque
$ss = \frac{2xy(x+y)^2}{(x-y)^2}$. Superest ergo ut $2xy$ fiat quadratum. Sumatur $x = 2qq$ et $y = rr$ fietque
$ss = \frac{4qqrr(2qq+rr)^2}{(2qq-rr)^2}$, ideoque $s = \frac{2qr(2qq+rr)}{2qq-rr}$, hincque $p = \frac{4qqrr}{2qq+rr}$,
indeque $x = 2qq$, $y = rr$, $z = \frac{pp(2qq+rr)}{2qqrr-pp}$, vel $z = \frac{8qqrr(2qq+rr)}{(2qq-rr)^2}$.
Exemplum casus primi. Sit $g = 2$ et $f = 1$, erit $s = \frac{2.3.20.17}{13}k$, $q = 3$, $r = 20$, $p = 17^2 k$, $x = 2.9\,k$,
$y = 2.20^2 k$, $z = \frac{818.17^4 k^3}{409.13^2 kk}$, vel $z = \frac{2.17^4 k}{13^2}$, hinc
$a = \frac{x}{s} = \frac{3.13}{17.20}$, $b = \frac{y}{s} = \frac{13.20}{3.17}$, $c = \frac{z}{s} = \frac{17^3}{3.13.20}$,
quorum productum est $\frac{13.17}{3.20}$ et summa . . . . falsa!
p. 122 - 127.

methods.what: Substitution $x=nqq$, $y=nrr$ reducing the equation to a ratio condition
methods.quote:

methods.what: Case n=2k: make $qq+rr-4qr$ a square by setting its root to $q+\frac{f}{g}r$, giving a parametric solution
Resulting formula for s in Case I
Case n=k: make $qq+rr-qr$ a square, parametrization
methods.quote: Sumatur ergo $q = gg - ff$ et $r = gg + 2fg$

methods.what: Alternative: choose $p=2xy/(x+y)$ so that $2xy$ must be a square; take $x=2qq$, $y=rr$
Numerical example of Case I with g=2, f=1

items.english: It remains therefore that $2xy$ become a square.
